Analyzing codegraph-bin AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard sources from the project's official GitHub repository, using predictable URLs based on the declared `pkgver`. The `source` array fetches the LICENSE file and a prebuilt binary archive for either x86_64 or aarch64, depending on the architecture. The checksums are explicitly provided and non-SKIPped, which enhances confidence in the integrity of the downloaded binaries, though even if they were skipped, that alone would not make this unsafe for this narrow gate.

The only executable code in the global scope or `pkgver()` function is the `latestver()` function, which uses `curl` and `jq` to fetch the latest release tag from GitHub's API. However, this function is not invoked anywhere in the PKGBUILD during the `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` or `makepkg --printsrcinfo` commands. It is defined but not called, so no network request is made during sourcing. Therefore, no unintended remote code execution or data exfiltration occurs.

All variable assignments and source definitions are static or based on known, deterministic expansions. There is no command substitution, eval, or obfuscated code in the top-level scope. The `package()` function contains logic that would run later during a full build, but it is irrelevant for this safety gate since `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` prevent it from executing. Thus, sourcing the PKGBUILD and downloading sources pose no risk of malicious execution.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>No dangerous execution during source fetch</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- No dangerous execution during source fetch

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a standard Arch Linux package build for `codegraph-bin`, a pre-indexed code knowledge graph tool. It fetches release binaries from the project's official GitHub repository (`https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph`) over HTTPS, which is a trusted source consistent with the package's declared upstream. The sources are versioned by release tag `v${pkgver}`, and checksums (sha256sums) are provided for both the license file and architecture-specific binaries, ensuring integrity.

The build process extracts and installs prebuilt binaries, places them under `/usr/lib/codegraph`, and creates a wrapper script in `/usr/bin/codegraph` to invoke the bundled Node.js executable with the main JS file. It also performs harmless post-processing: removing shebang lines from bundled JavaScript files (a common step when vendoring Node.js apps) and pruning empty directories. These operations are confined to the package directory and do not affect the host system.

No network requests, file operations, or command executions occur during `package()` that are outside the scope of standard packaging. There is no use of `eval`, no obfuscated code, and no downloading or executing of remote content during installation. The package follows typical AUR packaging practices and poses no evidence of malicious behavior.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR packaging with verified upstream binaries
</summary>
</security_assessment>

[1/2] Reviewing .SRCINFO...
+ Reviewed PKGBUILD. Status: SAFE -- Standard AUR packaging with verified upstream binaries
LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It lists the package name, version, source URLs, checksums, dependencies, and other relevant information. All sources point to the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph) and are versioned under release tags (v1.6.0). The source URLs for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures point to prebuilt binaries hosted on GitHub Releases, which is a common practice for `-bin` packages.

Checksums (sha256sums) are provided for all sources, including the LICENSE file, and are not set to 'SKIP', indicating that the sources are pinned and verified. The package depends only on standard system libraries (bash, glibc, libgcc, libstdc++.so), which are expected for a binary executable. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious scripts, or network operations outside the declared sources. The metadata aligns with standard AUR packaging practices for a binary distribution.

No executable code or commands are present in this file — it is purely declarative. As such, there is no mechanism here for data exfiltration, remote code execution, or other malicious behaviors. The package provides a local AI coding assistant tool with no indication of injected or unauthorized modifications.
</details>
<evidence>

Standard AUR metadata with verified sources; no malicious content</summary>
